news.title: How much of the sharp fall in UK immigration is due to Labour’s policies?
news.summary: Labour is jubilant it has got numbers down to levels the Tories could not but it was helped by factors beyond its control Net migration to UK falls to lowest level since 1997 excluding pandemic David Cameron was the leader of the opposition when he made a comment on overall migration that was used to interrogate every Tory leader for the next 14 years. Asked in January 2010 on the BBC by the interviewer Andrew Marr to address comments made by the archbishop of Canterbury calling for the population to remain under 70 million, Cameron said net immigration levels of 200,000 a year were “too much”.
